Routing notes:
- Do not assume option C is valid for every east-region request; it was rejected frequently.
- Confirm the exact request type and available options before selecting. Shipments (REQ-2403–2405, REQ-2408) consistently rejected C.
- Observed successful C assignments:
  - Transfer with “client has been asking twice” (REQ-2402)
  - Refund with the same wording (REQ-2406)
  - Transfer with “second attempt, first form bounced” (REQ-2407)
- The same wording/request combinations were not consistently predictive: transfer/client-asking-twice (REQ-2400) and refund/client-asking-twice (REQ-2409) rejected C; refund/second-attempt (REQ-2401) also rejected C.
- Sender department and region alone do not determine the correct option; identical or similar cases had different outcomes.
- When C is explicitly absent or truncated from the listed choices, avoid selecting it. Prefer A or B based on the complete ticket details.

Routing notes:
- Do not infer the correct option from region, department, request type, sender, or wording alone. Similar/identical cases have produced different valid options and outcomes.
- Always inspect the complete option list; do not select C when it is absent or truncated. If C is unavailable, choose A or B only from the full ticket context.
- Recent evidence further confirms inconsistency:
  - Shipment + “same as last month”: A rejected (REQ-2410), but A accepted (REQ-2417).
  - Renewal + “second attempt, first form bounced”: B accepted (REQ-2412), but B rejected (REQ-2419).
  - Transfer + “came in through the regional office”: A accepted (REQ-2413), B accepted (REQ-2415).
  - Claim + “client asking twice”: B rejected (REQ-2414), while earlier similar cases had differing results.
  - Renewal + “no rush, confirm receipt”: A rejected (REQ-2416); claim with same wording accepted using A (REQ-2411).
- Earlier observations still apply: shipments frequently rejected C (REQ-2403–2405, REQ-2408), but this is not proof that A or B is universally correct.
- Previously successful C cases (REQ-2402, REQ-2406, REQ-2407) do not establish a reliable rule; comparable wording/request combinations were rejected.
- Treat each ticket as an independent classification. Verify request details, exact available options, and any distinguishing context before selecting.

Routing notes:
- Treat every ticket as an independent classification. Do not infer the answer from region, department, request type, sender, or wording alone; similar cases have produced different valid options.
- Inspect the complete option list before deciding. Never choose an absent or truncated option. If C is unavailable, use the full ticket context to distinguish A/B.
- Recent evidence reinforces inconsistency:
  - “No rush, but please confirm receipt”: transfer rejected C (REQ-2420), refund accepted A (REQ-2424); renewal earlier rejected A (REQ-2416), while claim accepted A (REQ-2411).
  - “Same as last month”: shipment rejected A (REQ-2422; also REQ-2410), transfer rejected A (REQ-2426), though shipment A was accepted in REQ-2417.
  - “Scanned, not typed”: invoice rejected A (REQ-2421), transfer accepted A (REQ-2429).
  - Claim follow-up wording: “anything missing” rejected B (REQ-2423); “asking twice” rejected A (REQ-2427), with prior differing outcomes (REQ-2414).
  - Renewal “second attempt, first form bounced”: B accepted (REQ-2428 and REQ-2412), but other renewal B cases were rejected (REQ-2419, REQ-2425).
  - Transfer “regional office” wording previously allowed both A and B (REQ-2413, REQ-2415).
- Shipments frequently reject C (REQ-2403–2405, REQ-2408), but this is not a universal rule. Prior successful C cases (REQ-2402, REQ-2406, REQ-2407) do not establish a reliable pattern.
- Verify request details, exact options, and any distinguishing context for each ticket; do not generalize from wording alone.

  - “Scanned, not typed” accepted A for transfer (REQ-2432, REQ-2433, REQ-2439; also REQ-2429), but invoice rejected A (REQ-2421).

  - Claim “anything missing” accepted A (REQ-2437) but previously rejected B (REQ-2423). “Asking twice” previously rejected A.
  - Renewal urgency (“before end of day”) accepted B (REQ-2431); “second attempt, first form bounced” also accepted B, though other renewal B cases were rejected.

- Shipments frequently reject C, but successful C cases exist; never treat this as universal.

Routing notes:
- Treat every ticket as an independent classification. Do not infer the answer from region, department, sender, request type, or wording alone; similar wording can map to different options.
- Inspect the complete option list before deciding. Never choose an absent or truncated option. Verify request type, exact options, and distinguishing context each time.
- Wording is not a reliable universal rule:
  - “No rush, but please confirm receipt” accepted A for claims and refunds, but transfer rejected C; renewal previously rejected A.
  - “Scanned, not typed” accepted A for transfers and claims (REQ-2449), while claim B was rejected (REQ-2448) and invoice A was rejected.
  - “Same as last month” accepted B for invoice; shipment and transfer examples varied.
  - “Anything missing” accepted A for claim previously, but renewal accepted B (REQ-2440).
  - “Before end of day” accepted B for renewal (REQ-2431, REQ-2446), but was rejected for another renewal (REQ-2443).
  - “Through the regional office” accepted B for renewal (REQ-2441), but claim C was rejected (REQ-2447); claim history also rejected B.
  - “Asking twice” accepted B for shipment (REQ-2444), contradicting prior shipment examples rejecting A.
- Claims: recent evidence supports A for “no rush,” “scanned, not typed,” and possibly “anything missing”; do not generalize beyond the exact context. Regional-office wording rejected C and previously rejected B.
- Renewals: recent accepted choices are B for “anything missing,” regional-office wording, and some urgency cases; urgency is inconsistent, so inspect all context.
- Shipments frequently reject C, but successful C cases exist; “asking twice” most recently accepted B. Never treat any pattern as universal.

Routing notes:

- Wording is not a universal rule. Use prior outcomes only as request-specific evidence:
  - Claims: A accepted for “no rush, but please confirm receipt” and “scanned, not typed”; A also accepted for “anything missing.” Regional-office wording rejected C and previously B.
  - Transfers: A accepted for “scanned, not typed”; regional-office wording rejected C.
  - Shipments: A accepted for “anything missing.” Regional-office wording rejected C in multiple recent cases (REQ-2450, REQ-2459), though successful C cases exist. “Asking twice” previously accepted B; do not generalize.
  - Renewals: B accepted for “anything missing,” regional-office wording, some urgency cases, and “second attempt, first form bounced” (REQ-2458). Urgency remains inconsistent.
  - Refunds: B rejected for both “asking twice” (REQ-2451) and “before end of day” (REQ-2456); do not transfer shipment or renewal patterns to refunds.
  - Invoices: B rejected for “scanned, not typed” (REQ-2454); this conflicts with transfer/claim outcomes.
- “Same as last month,” “anything missing,” urgency, regional-office wording, and repeated requests must be evaluated within the exact request type and full context.

Routing notes:

- Inspect the complete, untruncated option list and exact request type before choosing. Never select an absent option. Confirm distinguishing context each time.
- Evidence is request-specific and sometimes inconsistent:
  - Claims: A accepted “no rush, but please confirm receipt” and “anything missing”; A previously accepted “scanned, not typed,” but was rejected for that wording in REQ-2469. Do not generalize; verify full context/options.
  - Transfers: A accepted “scanned, not typed” and “anything missing”; regional-office wording rejected C previously.
  - Shipments: A accepted “anything missing”; regional-office wording rejected C in REQ-2450/2459, though C has also succeeded. “Asking twice” previously mapped B. “Same as last month” rejected A in REQ-2467.
  - Renewals: B accepted “anything missing,” regional-office wording, some urgency cases, “second attempt,” and “scanned, not typed” (REQ-2464). Urgency remains inconsistent.
  - Refunds: A accepted “anything missing” and “second attempt” (REQ-2462/2463). Regional-office wording rejected A and B (REQ-2461/2468), indicating C when available. Earlier B rejections for “asking twice” and “before end of day” remain relevant.
  - Invoices: A rejected for “before end of day” and “scanned, not typed” (REQ-2460/2465); earlier B rejected for “scanned, not typed.” Do not assume a stable mapping.
  - Claims: regional-office wording previously rejected C.
- “Same as last month,” “anything missing,” urgency, regional-office wording, and repeated requests must be evaluated within the exact request type and complete ticket context.

- Renewals: anything missing, regional-office wording, second attempt, scanned/not typed, and same as last month → B. Urgency remains inconsistent.
- Refunds: anything missing and second attempt → A (REQ-2495). Regional-office wording → C rejected (REQ-2498), despite earlier C indications; do not assume C. Before-end-of-day → C rejected (REQ-2492), with earlier B rejection also recorded. Asking twice and urgency have produced rejections.

- Claims: “no rush, but confirm receipt” → A; “anything missing” → A.
- Transfers: scanned/not typed, same as last month, regional-office wording, and before-end-of-day → A.
- Shipments: second attempt → B; before-end-of-day → B.
- Renewals: before-end-of-day → B; regional-office wording → B.
- Refunds: anything missing and second attempt → A.
- Invoices: scanned/not typed → C.

Recent rejections/corrections:
- Shipment: scanned/not typed → A rejected; “anything missing” → A rejected. Earlier A indications are not reliable.
- Invoice: asking twice → A rejected; second attempt → A rejected.
- Refund: scanned/not typed → A rejected; regional-office wording → C rejected; before-end-of-day → C rejected. Earlier C/B indications remain unreliable.
- Renewal: same as last month → B rejected.
- Urgency is inconsistent across request types; do not map it automatically to B or another option.
- Regional-office wording is inconsistent: rejected for shipments/refunds, accepted as B for a renewal.
- “Same as last month” is inconsistent and recently rejected for a renewal.
- Several option lists were visibly truncated in the record; rely only on the complete options shown in the live ticket.

Recent accepted outcomes:
- Claims: “no rush, but confirm receipt,” “anything missing,” and “same as last month” → A.
- Transfers: scanned/not typed, same as last month, regional-office wording, and before-end-of-day → A.
- Shipments: second attempt and before-end-of-day → B.
- Renewals: before-end-of-day, regional-office wording, and scanned/not typed → B.
- Refunds: anything missing and second attempt → A.
- Invoices: scanned/not typed → C.

Recent rejections/corrections:
- Shipment: scanned/not typed and “anything missing” → A rejected.
- Invoice: asking twice and second attempt → A rejected; second attempt → B also rejected; regional-office wording → C rejected; “same as last month” → A rejected.
- Refund: scanned/not typed → A rejected; regional-office wording → C rejected; before-end-of-day → C rejected; “same as last month” → A rejected.
- Renewal: same as last month → B rejected.
- Earlier indications for these rejected combinations are unreliable.
- Regional-office wording varies by request type: rejected for shipments/refunds/invoices, accepted as B for a renewal.
- “Same as last month” is inconsistent: accepted for a claim, rejected for a renewal, refund, and invoice.
